name: Today's Report
headline: A month of rising mortgage rates adds $355 a month to the payment on the typical local home.
teaser: We will skip the daily rate recap and put the month in dollars instead. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fixed was 6.89% on Sept. 8 and 7.50% Thursday, after a high of 7.61% on Oct. 5. sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
We will skip the daily rate recap and put the month in dollars instead. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fixed was 6.89% on Sept. 8 and 7.50% Thursday, after a high of 7.61% on Oct. 5. On the five city median list price of $1,075,000 with 20% down, that moves principal and interest from $5,658 a month to $6,013, $355 more for the same home. Put the other way, the Sept. 8 payment now borrows about $51,000 less.

One correction: Market Briefs said rates "jumped (again)" to 7.5%. Thursday's 7.50% was a 0.09 point drop from Wednesday's 7.59%, MND's biggest one day decline in three months.

Locally, the five city ledger reads 687, up from 682. Milpitas rose to 103 from 101, and Fremont, Hayward and Newark each added one, to 241, 191 and 90; Union City held at 62. The board wide table rose to 2,670 from 2,656.

What this means for you: buyers holding a preapproval from early September should have it rerun, because the same payment now qualifies for about 6% less loan. Sellers should note the 147 homes that have sat 60 days or longer; most came on the market when the 30-year was under 6.9%.

  • Board wide: 2,670 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 148 coming soon and 201 brand new.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Live ledger: 687 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 615 are on the market and 72 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 241 live, 198 active, 27 coming soon and 16 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,274,944 at $797 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 31 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 191, Milpitas 103, Newark 90, Union City 62.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,075,000 at $675 a square foot. 290 homes are priced under a million, and 147 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

On the five city median list price of $1,075,000 with 20% down, the monthly principal and interest went from $5,658 to $6,013, up $355, and the Sept. 8 payment now borrows about $51,000 less.

images.source: Source: Mortgage News Daily daily rate index, as of Oct. 8, 2026. Payment is principal and interest on $1,075,000, the five city median list price in our Oct. 9 MLS export, with 20% down.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
A New York Fed study puts a number on tariffs. By February, tariffs had added about 2.9 percentage points to goods inflation: goods prices rose 2.0% over the year, and the authors estimate they would have fallen about 0.9% without tariffs. The study covers 67 categories of consumer goods other than oil, about three quarters of that spending.

Layoffs remain rare, but moods are slipping. First time jobless claims fell to 197,000 in the week ending Oct. 3, the lowest since July. On Friday the University of Michigan's preliminary October consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 from 48.1, and year ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6%.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Thursday's AI selloff hit Oracle and CoreWeave hardest. Oracle fell 5.48% and CoreWeave 7.77% after OpenAI, a major customer of both, put its revenue at about $50 billion a year, short of the $68 billion investors had heard.

Their year tells two very different stories. CoreWeave, which rents out AI computing power, is up 13.9% for 2026 after being up as much as 92.7% in May. Oracle, which is borrowing heavily to build AI data centers, is down 30.4%, and was down 41% at its July low. Both trail the Nasdaq's 17.0% gain. Early Friday, Oracle bounced more than 4%.

images.alt: Line chart of year to date stock performance in 2026 through the Oct. 8 close. CoreWeave is up 13.9% after a high of 92.7% on May 6. Oracle is down 30.4% after a low of minus 41.0% on July 24. The Nasdaq Composite, dashed, is up 17.0%.
images.caption: CoreWeave has kept a gain and Oracle has not, but both trail the Nasdaq's 17.0% this year.
images.source: Source: Yahoo Finance daily closes, Dec. 31, 2025 to Oct. 8, 2026. Price change only, dividends not included.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html:
Bitcoin is up 2.05% over 24 hours near $82,900, Ether up 2.53% and XRP up 2.36%, live from CoinGecko at 9:20 AM PT. Thursday Bitcoin fell 1.90% on Coinbase, to $81,693; Market Briefs printed it up 0.56%.

JPMorgan estimates about $50 billion has flowed into digital assets so far this year, counting funds, futures, venture money and company treasuries. Crypto ETF flows are positive for the year again after outflows in May and June, though the overall pace is still about half of last year's.
